writeup.headline: EverQuote rates Buy on strong growth, net cash and low absolute multiples, with a lukewarm price trend.
writeup.thesis: EverQuote scores 76, a Buy, four points short of Strong Buy. Growth is the main driver: TTM revenue growth of 22.8% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 24.6% year on year, with growth sped up by 10.0 pp from the previous quarter. The balance sheet scores 100 with net cash and no debt, and quality is solid with a 97.7% gross margin, 11.0% operating margin, 12.6% FCF margin and diluted share count down 4.9% year on year. Valuation is low in absolute terms at 1.0x sales, 8.2x FCF and 7.0x EV/EBIT, with FCF yield 7.3 pp above the 10-year Treasury yield, and is cheap against its own history (P/FCF not comparable). Holding the score back are a middling trend (price 22.9% below its 52-week high, shares down 6.6% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago) and a neutral-to-slightly-positive news score.
key_risks: Customer concentration: one customer made up 31% of Q2 revenue, so a pullback in carrier spending could hit results hard.
Insurance carrier advertising budgets are cyclical; demand could cool after the current growth push.
Competition in AI-driven insurance shopping, including Insurify, could pressure the new Luva brand and margins.
An open trademark suit from Solo Insurance Services remains unresolved.
Shares are 22.9% below their 52-week high and 4.2% below the 50-day average, so price momentum is weak.
what_would_change: A 4-point score gain would lift the rating to Strong Buy, for example from improving price trend or positive news around the November 2 results.
A drop of 12 points would push it to Hold, for example if growth slowed sharply or the share price trend deteriorated further.
Loss of share or budget cuts from the largest customer would weigh on growth and quality scores.
A sharp rerating upward in the share price would reduce the valuation score, which currently contributes strongly.
